title: SOURCE_TARGETS validated: REVOKE writes Grantor from pooled sys-session user state

payload.method_pivot: The generated grant target did not validate as pending TxnReadTS ingress because GrantExec uses a sys session and userExists uses restricted SQL without UseCurSession. Source inspection exposed a nearby stronger obligation: pooled sys-session state must not be used as user-visible privilege metadata.
payload.user_symptom: After user A grants table privileges to a target user, user B revokes only SELECT while leaving INSERT. The mysql.tables_priv row remains, but Grantor becomes empty instead of identifying the current privilege actor B.
payload.quality_gate: Medium-quality SQL-visible metadata bug. It is not a security-attack claim: the privilege set changes correctly, but the user-visible audit metadata in mysql.tables_priv.Grantor is wrong. Existing integration coverage already checks Grantor for GRANT, but not for REVOKE.

provenance.source: state-ingress dynamic target-analysis plus SQL-only testbed reproduction

title: SOURCE_TARGETS validated: REVOKE table privilege Grantor uses pooled sys-session User

payload.method_pivot: The revoke source target is the direct fault side of the grant/revoke validation. The target should not be re-executed as pending TxnReadTS ingress; it is covered by the pooled sys-session state isolation RED.
payload.user_symptom: After cross-user partial REVOKE, mysql.tables_priv keeps the remaining privilege row but Grantor is empty rather than the current revoker.
payload.quality_gate: Same SQL-visible metadata bug as the grant target pivot; the privilege set is correct, but Grantor metadata is written from the wrong session owner.

name: Pooled internal session state must not become user-visible statement metadata

query_pattern: code obtains a pooled sys/internal session
one path writes user-derived state into that sys session
ReleaseSysSession returns the session to the pool without restoring that state
another user-visible statement later reads state from the sys session to populate metadata or make an authorization-facing decision
code_markers: ReleaseSysSession rolls back and puts the resource but does not reset the field
a sibling executor obtains GetSysSession but does not initialize the same field
a compose/update helper writes a user-visible system table column from ctx.GetSessionVars() where ctx is the internal session
stop_rules: require a SQL-visible effect, not just a leaked in-memory field
prefer cross-user schedules where the expected current actor differs from the stale or default sys-session state
separate correctness metadata bugs from privilege-enforcement bugs; do not frame as a security issue unless authorization semantics actually change

provenance.source: validated grant/revoke Grantor RED on testbed 8220955

name: GRANT/REVOKE table privilege metadata through pooled sys sessions

state_model: GrantExec obtains a sys session and copies the outer session user into internalSession.GetSessionVars().User before privilege-table writes
ReleaseSysSession only rolls back and returns the sys session to the pool; it does not restore SessionVars.User
RevokeExec obtains a sys session but does not copy the outer session user into it
revokeTablePriv passes the internal session into composeTablePrivUpdateForRevoke
composeTablePrivUpdateForRevoke writes mysql.tables_priv.Grantor from ctx.GetSessionVars().User.String(), so ctx ownership decides user-visible metadata
existing integration tests verify Grantor for GRANT as root@%, confirming the field is user-visible test surface

pkg/executor/internal/exec/executor.go:581-591 ReleaseSysSession rollbacks and puts the sys session without resetting User
pkg/executor/revoke.go:78-83 RevokeExec gets a sys session without initializing User

name: REVOKE table privilege updates must record the current privilege actor in Grantor metadata

payload.p_check: RevokeExec uses a pooled sys session as the ctx passed to composeTablePrivUpdateForRevoke, and that helper writes Grantor from ctx.GetSessionVars().User.String().
payload.q_claim: If REVOKE updates mysql.tables_priv.Grantor, the value must come from the user executing the REVOKE statement, not from an uninitialized or stale pooled sys-session user field.
payload.fault: RevokeExec does not initialize the sys session User from the outer session before passing it to composeTablePrivUpdateForRevoke.

name: mysql.tables_priv Grantor reflects the actor of a table privilege metadata update

payload.contract: When a table privilege statement updates mysql.tables_priv.Grantor, the value should be derived from the current user executing that statement. An internal sys-session default or stale pooled value is not a valid user-visible Grantor.
minimal_observation: create two grant-capable users A and B plus target user C
A grants two table privileges to C so mysql.tables_priv retains a row and records Grantor=A
B revokes only one of the privileges so the row remains with the other privilege
RED if the row remains but Grantor is empty or identifies a session other than B

red_signature.before_lines: lines 91-95 show Grantor ai_grantor_a@% after A grants SELECT,INSERT
red_signature.after_lines: lines 104-109 show B revoked SELECT, the row remains with Insert, and Grantor is empty

controls: use two privileges and revoke only one so the mysql.tables_priv row is not deleted
use different A and B users so stale/default/current user states are distinguishable
query mysql.tables_priv directly because existing tests already treat Grantor as visible metadata for GRANT

name: Cross-user GRANT then partial REVOKE keeps table privilege row visible

payload.shape: Two grant-capable users operate on the same target user's table privilege row. The second operation revokes only one privilege so metadata remains observable.
payload.why_interesting: Single-user schedules can hide actor-metadata bugs because stale, default, and current user may be indistinguishable. Partial revoke avoids row deletion and exposes whether the executor used the outer session or a pooled internal session.
setup: A and B each have table privileges with GRANT OPTION
observations: after B revoke: expected current actor B if Grantor is rewritten; observed empty Grantor with Table_priv=Insert

name: Cross-user metadata schedule for pooled sys-session actor leaks

steps: create an object whose metadata records the current actor
create two users A and B that can both perform the metadata-updating operation
make A perform the first operation and query the metadata row
make B perform a partial inverse/update operation that leaves the metadata row visible
query the metadata row again and compare the actor field to B
red_conditions: the metadata actor field becomes empty
the metadata actor field remains A after B's operation
the metadata actor field identifies any user other than B
green_conditions: the same schedule records B after B's operation while preserving the intended privilege set

name: Revoke table-priv update uses pooled sys-session User as Grantor

payload.source_anchor: pkg/executor/revoke.go:300 and pkg/executor/revoke.go:398 pass internalSession into composeTablePrivUpdateForRevoke, then write Grantor from internalSession.GetSessionVars().User.String()

trigger_condition.phase: REVOKE table privilege updates a mysql.tables_priv row that will remain after the revoke
trigger_condition.state: the current SQL user is different from the sys session's User field
trigger_condition.fault: RevokeExec never copies e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().User into internalSession before composing Grantor metadata

observe: A grants SELECT,INSERT and Grantor is ai_grantor_a@%
the row remains with Table_priv=Insert but Grantor is empty on testbed 8220955
payload.fix_shape: Use the outer user session as the source of Grantor for REVOKE metadata, or initialize and restore the sys session User with a scoped guard before using helpers that read SessionVars.User.

lessons.selector_worked_but_pivoted: The original grant source target was not a TxnReadTS ingress bug. Following the state ownership proof obligation found a sibling pooled-sys-session metadata bug in REVOKE.
lessons.oracle_strength: A cross-user schedule and partial revoke converted a subtle in-memory ownership issue into a SQL-visible metadata RED.
